title: A Real Screenshot Can Still Mislead You

scenes.speaker: Alex
scenes.text: A screenshot can be real—and still mislead you.

scenes.speaker: Maya
scenes.text: Try this made-up example. Crop a sentence after “I agree,” and hide the part that says “with neither claim.”

scenes.speaker: Alex
scenes.text: Same words. Different meaning. Now imagine a post accusing Jewish people of something, using one cropped quote as the whole argument.

scenes.speaker: Maya
scenes.text: Before sharing it, open the original. Who said it? When? What came before and after? Are we seeing a quote, a translation, or somebody’s caption?

scenes.speaker: Alex
scenes.text: Then check an independent source. And even if one person really said something awful, that does not make an entire community responsible.

scenes.speaker: Maya
scenes.text: Context isn’t an excuse. It’s how you figure out what actually happened, and who actually did it.

scenes.speaker: Alex
scenes.text: Zoom out before you call it proof.
scenes.on_screen: ZOOM OUT BEFORE YOU CALL IT PROOF
scenes.source: Beyond the Myth · Facts, not scapegoats
